notes.4a: Most candidates were able to make a reasonable sketch of the graph of y =e 2 , however the graph of y = x5 proved to be more difficult to sketch for some candidates. notes.4b: Most candidates were able to gain marks from the correct use of the iteration process, obtaining iterations correct to 6 significant figures, however some candidates either truncated their answer or did not give the final result to the correct level of accuracy.
notes.5: Most candidates obtained some marks by recognising the need for implicit differentiation and that the term 4e2xy needed to be differentiated as a product. Some candidates made errors in the simplification of their derivative and so did not obtain a correct result. Another common error was to omit the differentiation of the constant term 21.
notes.6a: It was pleasing to see that there were many completely correct solutions, usually using algebraic long division, which clearly showed both the quotient and the remainder. Some candidates chose to use synthetic division, which was acceptable provided an adjustment to division by was made when dealing with the quotient. Unfortunately, some candidates did not do this and gave an incorrect quotient of 12x2 +8x.
notes.6b: Most candidates realised that they needed to make use of the response to part (a), obtaining an integrand of 2+ . notes.7a: Most candidates realised that differentiation of a quotient was needed and were able to obtain a correct derivative. Problems arose when candidates did not realise that at the point A, the value of x is 1, and it was this value that was needed to be used in the derivative.
notes.7b: Few correct responses were seen, with many candidates using the equation of the curve rather than the equation of gradient function. It was expected that a substitution of x =3 and x =3.1 be made into the gradient function, showing a change of sign which implied that the point B was a maximum point.
notes.7c: Some candidates chose to make use of two separate trapezia to calculate an approximate area for the shaded region. notes.general_comments:
It was evident that many candidates were well prepared for the examination and were able to produce a
range of clear and well thought out solutions. It was also evident that there were some candidates who were
not so well prepared as evidenced by incomplete or questions that were not attempted. There appeared to
be no timing issues and most candidates had sufficient room on the script, making use of the additional
sheet when needed.
